newsitem.title: USA: FAA orders Los Angeles to return airport funds.
newsitem.headline: FAA orders Los Angeles to return airport funds.

text.p: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has ordered Los Angeles to return $30.3 million to the Los Angeles Department of Airports because the funds were improperly transferred, a spokesman said Tuesday.

Until the city repays the money, the FAA will freeze $60 million in federal grants for capital improvements at four airports that Los Angeles operates, U.S. Department of Transportation spokesman Bill Schulz said.
An investigation by the FAA had determined that the $30.3 million should be "promptly returned to the airport account because it was improperly transferred," he said.
The FAA determined that the Los Angeles funds transfer violated a federal law that requires that airport revenues be spent on airport operations, Schulz said.

Last November, the Los Angeles City Council voted to hold the funds in a city trust account until the issue was resolved. At the time, City Councilman Nate Holden warned that the council decision could spark a legal battle with the FAA.
Los Angeles City Controller Rick Tuttle was not immediately available for comment on Tuesday.
Tuttle has said the airport funds were repayment for past investments by the city for fire safety and certain public works projects at the airport.
